messages:
marisa: FYI opened support case NEB-2245 — customer says they completed SSO onboarding but there is no API key visible in their project. Console shows a key, but when they call the API it 403s and the admin UI indicates the key is bound to project "redwood-internal". Customer wants a repro & quick fix. attaching snippets they sent.

dan: I can repro locally. Quick steps I ran: 1) OIDC sign-in -> 2) provisioner POST /provision/claim -> 3) API returns 202 and provision job succeeds, but key appears in internal project. Short log excerpt: 
```
provisioner: received claim org=nebulaapps user=alice@nebula timestamp=2026-02-08T14:22:11Z
provisioner: resolved tenant_id=svc-internal-01 via mapper fallback
provisioner: created api_key id=ak_01HXYZ bound_project=proj-internal-000
```

support-bot: Provisioner job 48f2c completed (duration 3.1s) :eyes:

henrik: That tenant_id resolution line stands out — looks like the mapper fell back to a default internal tenant because the claim.mapped_org was empty. We had a similar transient bug when the partner-connector returned a 204. Possible causes: (a) race in mapping cache refresh, (b) missing org claim in OIDC payload.

marisa: Customer says their IdP includes the org claim. They also forwarded our webhook payload where org_slug=nebulaapps is present. So either our mapping lookup failed or we picked the wrong mapping during provision. They need keys to work in prod today. Any safe hotfix?

dan: Two paths: (1) manual rebind of the api_key to the correct project (fast, manual DB/admin action), (2) re-run provisioner with forced rebind which is safer for audit but takes longer. If we manual rebind we should rotate the key afterwards.

henrik: Agreed. Manual rebind procedure (admin only):
```
# query current binding
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://admin.internal/api/keys/ak_01HXYZ
# rebind to project
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"bind_project":"proj-neb-123"}' https://admin.internal/api/keys/ak_01HXYZ/rebind
# rotate key
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://admin.internal/api/keys/ak_01HXYZ/rotate
```
Note: rotation invalidates old key so coordinate with customer to update secrets. Also preserve audit entries: include a note referencing ticket NEB-2245.

marisa: I'll ask customer if they accept manual rebind + rotation. If yes, I'll perform rebind during their agreed maintenance window to minimize disruption.

dan: If we need to re-run the provisioner instead: run `provisioner reconcile --org nebulaapps --force-rebind --dry-run` first to validate. If output looks good, drop `--dry-run`. That will create a new binding and mark the created key as orphaned for rotation.

henrik: Created infra ticket INFRA-992 to add a guard: provisioner should fail fast if mapper returns a fallback internal tenant and emit an alert. We'll also add a short-term metric for keys created in "internal" projects to catch recurrence. Linking ticket to NEB-2245.

marisa: Customer approved manual rebind + rotate, scheduled for 2026-02-08 16:30 UTC. Executing now.

dan: After rebind & rotate, test output: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <new_key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` -> 200 OK. I confirmed token accepted and model list returns correctly.

marisa: Updated customer, they verified calls succeed. Closing loop on the case. Filing internal postmortem note in NEB-2245 with steps and INFRA-992 link. :white_check_mark:

henrik: Thanks — followups: add unit test for mapper fallback behavior, and add an alert rule for >0 keys created in internal projects per 24h.

dan: I'll add the test to eng-infra backlog.

marisa: Closing thread; will paste long logs & screenshots into the ticket.
